children: MIXED RESPONSE TO EARLY US EARNINGS REPORTS
The third-quarter US earnings season is under way now with the release this morning of results from some key banks including JPMorgan
and Goldman Sachs
Shares of the banks that had reported are mixed, with Citigroup
down nearly 4% even as the bank beat Wall Street estimates for third-quarter profit. All three of the major US indexes are down modestly in afternoon trading.
Analysts were expecting S&P 500
CBOE:SPX
companies as of Friday to increase earnings in the third quarter by 30.6% from a year ago, with year-over-year financials
earnings seen up 4.9%, according to LSEG.
S&P 500 revenue for the quarter was seen up 11.8% from a year ago.
"Following big positive surprises in the last two quarters, healthy beats are the status quo and may not be enough to drive stocks higher,"  BofA Securities strategists wrote in a note this week.
Investor focus will largely be on AI-related growth, with tech
company earnings expected to grow 66.5% in the quarter from a year ago and communication services
earnings seen up 47.8% year-over-year. Energy
earnings, meanwhile, are seen up 123% year-over-year, based on LSEG data.
Main US indexes modestly red
Healthcare is the weakest S&P 500 sector; energy leads gainers
Euro STOXX 600 index off ~0.1%
Dollar falls; gold dips; US crude, bitcoin rise modestly
US 10-year Treasury yield edges down to ~5.22%
